📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City and Russell Martin are in far better form, with Rangers and Simon Jordan now part of an interesting story developing in recent months now that things are finally looking up for the Foxes.

Their 1-0 away victory over Huddersfield Town was arguably one of the most impressive results anywhere in League One this season, suggesting Russell Martin's ideas are beginning to take hold with this Leicester City squad.

The former MK Dons, Swansea City, Southampton, and Rangers boss has now taken charge of five clubs, with Leicester representing his latest challenge. After a difficult start, he is beginning to show why the Foxes appointed him.

Martin's appointment at Leicester was always going to divide opinion, particularly after his disastrous 123-day spell at Rangers, where he won just five of his 17 matches before being dismissed.

He then endured a difficult start in the East Midlands, winning two and losing three of his first eight league fixtures. The pressure was considerable given Leicester's expectation of bouncing straight back to the Championship, with another season in League One representing a disaster for a club of their stature.

Recent findings suggest that simon Jordan was among those questioning Martin's position at Leicester, with things looking particularly bleak after the 3-1 defeat to Peterborough United and former Leicester player Robbie Savage. The warning was there that he would be sacked unless results improved.

Industry observers note that however, the Foxes have since won four of their next six league games, including that outstanding Huddersfield victory. Rangers supporters and some of the divisive coach’s other critics could be eating their words.

They have always piled on Martin for last season, with neither they nor Jordan perhaps enjoying seeing him turn things around. Leicester are looking considerably more positive, easy on the eye, and results are following.

Martin's Southampton side also took time to get going, suffering four consecutive defeats early in his first season before eventually embarking on a remarkable 25-match unbeaten run.

George Elek, an EFL expert and Not The Top 20 podcast pundit, has argued that Martin's reputation has become a footballing culture war, with his failures often attracting considerably more attention than his achievements.

It has been revealed that will Russell Martin return Leicester to the Championship at the first time of asking? Comment below!

Industry observers note that in further replies on X (formerly Twitter), Elek added: "Tough ask to expect him to come on board a sinking ship and turn it around straight away. League position at this stage is pretty meaningless, they’re clearly playing well now. Why do you think chucking money at it will solve the clear rot that had set in? His playing style is extreme. Is he not entitled to have some time to implement it?".

Recent findings suggest that there is a reasonable argument that Leicester simply needed to give him time to implement his ideas, particularly given the scale of the rebuilding job. The Foxes could now be ready to climb the table rapidly and become genuine automatic promotion contenders rather than simply hoping to sneak into the play-offs.

There is, however, a cautionary tale from Martin's Southampton tenure. Despite that extraordinary unbeaten run, Saints eventually fizzled out during the closing stages of the 2023/24 campaign, losing three games in one damaging April week and missing out on automatic promotion.

They entered the play-offs with questions surrounding their form, although they ultimately overcame Leeds at Wembley. Leicester would happily take that outcome, but should be wary of allowing their standards to drop once the initial momentum arrives.

Martin has the midfield quality to dominate League One for the foreseeable future, with John Lundstram, Sammy Braybrooke, Will Smallbone, and Louis Page offering an excellent blend of technical ability, energy and composure.

According to recent reports, that engine room could become the foundation of a serious promotion challenge from this point forth. Rangers fans and Jordan would not enjoy that turnaround, should it come to fruition.

#95565. Breaking: Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1456 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1456 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old stated last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most crucial players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another rapidly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

It has been revealed that inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler noted shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

According to recent reports, across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

But who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

In this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

According to recent reports, ‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer claims. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

According to recent reports, ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

During his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

According to recent reports, spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another crucial step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

According to recent reports, ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer says. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

Sources indicate that ‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

According to recent reports, the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

Sources indicate that ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he indicates. ‘He wants to achieve major things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

Recent findings suggest that ‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • Recent findings suggest that he needn’t have worried.
  • According to recent reports, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Recent findings suggest that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

According to recent reports, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

In a recent development, since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

It has been revealed that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola noted, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

It has been revealed that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

According to recent reports, “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose mentioned. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Sources indicate that speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

It has been revealed that jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has noted and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has noted that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he mentioned: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Recent findings suggest that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He stated: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most vital one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to newly introduced heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, mentioned: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

According to recent reports, liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Latest Update: Plymouth Argyle owners fired Bim Pepple transfer warning

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EFL pundits Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith have issued a warning to the Plymouth Argyle hierarchy after Tom Cleverley's side were defeated 2-0 by Peterborough United at Home Park without the attacking quality of Canadian forward, Bim Pepple.
  • Argyle's positive start to the League One season has hit stumbling block, with the home defeat to Robbie Savage's side following a heavy 3-0 defeat to Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough.
  • Harry Leonard's goal put the seal on things for Posh after his namesake, Harry Ashfield, opened the scoring midway through the first period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EFL pundits Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith have issued a warning to the Plymouth Argyle hierarchy after Tom Cleverley's side were defeated 2-0 by Peterborough United at Home Park without the attacking quality of Canadian forward, Bim Pepple.

Argyle's positive start to the League One season has hit stumbling block, with the home defeat to Robbie Savage's side following a heavy 3-0 defeat to Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough.

Harry Leonard's goal put the seal on things for Posh after his namesake, Harry Ashfield, opened the scoring midway through the first period.

Other results meant the Green Army dropped to seventh in the table, having taken 23 points from their opening 16 matches.

However, the growing concern surrounding Cleverley's men is their transfer strategy and lack of potential strength-in-depth, with the former Manchester United and England midfielder opting for a front two of Will Evans and Caleb Watts, with Pepple absent for just a third time this campaign.

Pepple moved to Home Park from Luton Town last summer in a deal which could rise as high as £600k, with the former Chesterfield loanee netting 16 times in just 35 League One appearances for the Pilgrims last term as Cleverley's men narrowly missed out on the play-offs.

The 23-year-old has scored five times so far this term, but was sidelined before the defeat to Sheffield Wednesday with a muscular problem.

Regardless, Cleverley backed his fellow attackers to step up to the plate and provide goals, but with blanks fired in the past 180 minutes' worth of action, questions have arisen on this particular front.

Pepple was one half of Argyle's formidable attacking duo last season, with Lorent Tolaj finding the net 21 times in his 35 appearances for the club, before the Swiss youth international was sold to Bristol City in a £4m deal.

Plymouth then sought to replace the 25-year-old with Evans, who is yet to replicate his prior Mansfield Town exploits after a £400,000 agreement, having netted just three times whilst starting in all of his upcoming employers' 16 league encounters.

Discussing a potential overreliance on Pepple, Fowler said on the Pyramid podcast: "They've got some good players, but they're screaming out for a 'proper' forward.

"Pepple didn't play in this (game). He's not there.

It has been revealed that "So, from what were your starting strikers last season in Tolaj and Pepple, both brilliant for this level. They've got Evans and Watts," he added.

"That's where your problem is, it's a lack of quality," Fowler claimed.

Recent findings suggest that plymouth fans, do you agree with this viewpoint of your club's attacking department? Comment below!

"I do think Plymouth's owners are trying to be as sustainable as possible.

"If you continue to sell your best players and try and replace them with a cheap option, you will just go down and down and down.

It has been revealed that "Plymouth aren't completely out of this run-in. Obviously, it depends on how long Pepple's out for, but it is a bit concerning losing 2-0 at home to Peterborough.".

The concerns raised by Fowler and Smith are particularly valid, both in the short and long-term, as it remains to be seen when Pepple returns from injury, as well as where he is playing his football in the coming months.

Several Championship sides have been credited with interest in his services, as well as Scottish Premiership side, Celtic, within the past 12 months, and it would be no surprise if the forward wanted to test himself regularly at second tier level after just 13 prior appearances.

With Evans and Watts only scoring five between them so far this season, it is apparent that Argyle may need to reinvest further in January if they are to keep pace with the many promotion hopefuls at the moment in League One, as only nine points separate Huddersfield Town in second and 13th-placed Mansfield right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that QPR were forced to leave the winger out of their squad for their trip to Carrow Road on Tuesday night. They went on to draw 1-1 in East Anglia against the Canaries with Harvey Vale getting their goal in the first-half.

Smyth, 29, has been ever-present for the Hoops so far this season under head coach Julien Stephan and he has enjoyed plenty of game time for the London outfit. He has made 16 appearances in all competitions, 15 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three goals and three assists.

In this latest update regarding his availability, West London Sport have claimed he wasn’t able to feature against Norwich City last time out due to an upset stomach. The R’s will be hoping he can recover over the next couple of days as they prepare for their home clash against Sheffield United on Saturday.

Sources indicate that QPR are sat in 7th place in the table after their first 17 fixtures. They are in the play-offs along with Stoke City, Birmingham City, Southampton and Swansea City.

In a recent development, QPR are well stocked up with players in their attacking department. Smyth started at Millwall last Saturday as the Hoops ran out 1-0 winners courtesy of Nicolas Madsen‘s first-half goal.

The R’s made a host of changes against Norwich City as they freshened things up. Koki Saito, Kwame Poku and the goal scorer Vale came into their starting XI in Smyth’s absence.

Smyth, who is a Northern Ireland international with 26 caps to his name, is an unsung hero for QPR. He is quick, tricky and has bags of experience in the EFL now.

It has been revealed that he has played over 350 games in his career to date and will be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room. The Linfield academy graduate has also had spells in the past at Accrington Stanley, Wycombe Wanderers, Charlton Athletic and Leyton Orient.

Sources indicate that QPR will need to assess Smyth ahead of their match against Sheffield United. They will be hoping that he can get better and be available for selection.

The forward gives the Hoops more competition and depth at the top end of the pitch. The R’s will be in confident mood right now and are four games unbeaten.

GdS: Possession vs. directness – key tactical differences between Milan and Frosinone

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.
  • Sources indicate that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

Sources indicate that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Recent findings suggest that amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That indicates in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

The shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

Sources indicate that in the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

The Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having mentioned all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

#95553. Kim Hellberg's new Middlesbrough transfer wish - Sunderland ace & 2 others must be eyed

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1038 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Kim Hellberg's new Middlesbrough transfer wish - Sunderland ace & 2 others must be eyed

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The January transfer window is closing in, and at Middlesbrough, Kim Hellberg has already revealed which position is their priority to strengthen.
  • Rokas Pukstas' start to life at the Riverside has yet to get into first gear.
  • It was revealed last week that the 21-year-old will have to go under the knife to repair it, and Boro boss Kim Hellberg has admitted that any first-team minutes between now and the end of the season will be a positive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The January transfer window is closing in, and at Middlesbrough, Kim Hellberg has already revealed which position is their priority to strengthen.

Rokas Pukstas' start to life at the Riverside has yet to get into first gear. He made a six-minute cameo against QPR before going down with a hamstring injury while training in America over the three-week international break back in September.

It was revealed last week that the 21-year-old will have to go under the knife to repair it, and Boro boss Kim Hellberg has admitted that any first-team minutes between now and the end of the season will be a positive.

The Swedish head coach also revealed that Rangers loanee Connor Barron is right now injured, but with no minutes in a Boro shirt since his arrival in the summer, it's almost all but certain that the Scottish giants will be considering bringing him back once the window opens.

Speaking after their 2-0 win over Bristol City last Saturday, Hellberg remarked that it was "absolute" that Middlesbrough needed to strengthen their midfield, with it likely that Sebastian Berhalter and Aidan Morris will be their only senior central midfielders come the end of the calendar year.

Here are three players they should be targetting.

We'll start with arguably the more underwhelming choice, but one that would ensure continuity and familiarity within the squad and wouldn't put too much pressure on replacing Morris or Berhalter, who are becoming quite an established duo in the engine room.

Alan Browne spent last season on loan at Middlesbrough from Sunderland, playing the utility role to perfection. The Irishman played a range of positions in midfield and even covered across the backline when needed.

Various injuries to key players effectively made him a first-choice player from mid-January until the end of the season, and he played the full 90 minutes in their play-off final defeat to Hull City back in May.

Since returning to the Stadium of Light, Browne hasn't featured in competitions that the Black Cats care about. His only bows have come in the EFL Cup and the EFL Trophy. He's yet to make a squad in the Europa League, and finally made his first Premier League 20 in their goalless draw with Aston Villa on Saturday.

There were murmurs back in September about him possibly having his contract paid out, and if Boro could bring him back for free, he'd be a useful addition.

Even so, with his deal set to expire in the summer, the 31-year-old shouldn't be available for too much in January if he's still under contract on Wearside.

Barnsley are in some real dire straits at the moment, battling down at the bottom of League One.

January will be crucial if Daniel Stendel's side are going to avoid a first fourth-tier campaign since the late 1970s, but there's the possibility that they could be looking even worse come the time the window slams shut.

Despite the Tykes' position, they still have some quality amongst the squad, and there's a strong possibility that the unpopular ownership group at Oakwell could cash in on the likes of Reyes Cleary or, in this case, Patrick Kelly, as they'd be worth a lot less as League Two footballers in the summer if that's where they end up.

Cleary gets a lot of the plaudits amongst neutrals, given how impressive he was last season, but, arguably, Kelly has been Barnsley's best player so far this term.

Sources indicate that the Northern Irish international has run the show from midfield. Only Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Oliver Norwood have created more chances from open play in League One, and only the Huddersfield Town wideman and Will Alves have created more chances as a result of them carrying the ball forward.

Kelly has excelled in the high-octane, pressing style that Stendel has deployed at Barnsley this season, so he shouldn't have to adapt too much to what Hellberg would want him to do, which may have been the issue for Leo Castledine this time last season.

And as a chance creator, he could deputise in the Riley McGree role behind the striker if needs be, too.

Middlesbrough have found joy in scouting from the MLS and looking at American midfielders, so if a latest middle-man is needed at the Riverside in January, it wouldn't be wild to take a look at some of the better-performing Americans in the division in 2026.

17-year-old Adri Mehmeti would be a dream signing by the looks of things, but realistically, whoever comes in will likely initially be playing understudy to their two compatriots already in the middle at the Riverside.

Recent findings suggest that 23-year-old Beau Leroux of the San Jose Earthquakes could be considered, though. The defensive midfielder initially looks like a bit of a disruptor, like Morris can be.

Do you think there are other MLS gems who Middlesbrough could target this January? Let us know in the comments.

The Boro man has made more tackles and won possession more times than anyone in the Championship so far this season, per Opta. In the 2026 MLS campaign, Leroux was 8th in duels won, 10th in possession won and 25th in tackles made.

Per FotMob, the 23-year-old was a top 10% defensive midfielder in defensive contributions, recoveries and possession won in the final third, and in the top 1% for duels won.

Recent findings suggest that so, defensively, he looks to be a strong candidate, but he can also bring something in the attacking and chance-creating sense, too. He scored four and assisted seven in 33 MLS games last season, taking 52 shots from defensive midfield and creating 37 chances.

In a recent development, leroux's ceiling looks quite high, and there is room for improvement. His pass percentage numbers weren't much to shout about, so if he does come in, he would seemingly be someone to learn from Morris and Berhalter, who look to do either side of the game better than he does right now.

However, if he can realise his potential under Helberg, he could become a real all-action box-to-box midfielder who could cope with the Premier League, which is Middlesbrough's ultimate goal come the end of this season.

Tech Report: Harry Kane's injury blow: Ballon d'Or winner sends upbeat message from hospital amid England concerns captain will be out for MONTHS after tearing ligaments

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:58 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 10:47 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne - with the striker revealing he will only return for 'the business end of the season'.
  • Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:58 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 10:47 EST, 21 November 2026.

Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne - with the striker revealing he will only return for 'the business end of the season'.

Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.

The defender had won the ball but caught Kane with his follow through on his ankle.

Kane had initially tried to play on after treatment, before eventually needing to be replaced.

The Ballon d'Or winner was upbeat on Saturday morning however, sharing a message with his fans that stressed his readiness to come back better than ever.

'The highs and lows of life!' Kane captioned a picture of himself wearing a protective boot. 'Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going in 2027.

Harry Kane was forced off during Bayern Munich's draw against Cologne on Friday night.

Bayern confirmed the England captain is set to be out for months following the injury.

But despite his injury, Kane was upbeat as he spoke to fans for the first time on Saturday (Source: Harry Kane/X).

'I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

'"Tough times don't last, tough people do" - my guy (Julian Edelman) told me this one!' Kane added, quoting the NFL icon.

Industry observers note that 'Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut (red heart emoji, strong arm emoji).'.

Speaking post-match, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl revealed that Kane has suffered ligament damage.

A Bayern club statement confirmed the blow, reading: 'Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

'This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department.

Sources indicate that 'The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months. Get well soon Harry.'.

Kane's absence will be a major blow for Bayern, with the Ballon d'Or winner having scored ten goals in 16 matches so far this season.

Bayern, who are already without Luis Diaz, Saibari and Serge Gnabry, also saw Michael Olise come off at half-time.

The German giants later confirmed Olise had suffered a 'contusion of the forefoot', with the Frenchman set to undergo treatment in the coming days.

It remains to be seen whether Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week when making his 126th appearance in the 2-1 win over Croatia - is at risk of missing the Nations League quarter-final against Norway in March.

Vincent Kompany, who was back in the dugout for the first time since his collapse last month, admitted other players will have to step up for Bayern in the absence of star names such as Kane.

'These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now,' Kompany noted, as per Bild.

'We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern.

Bayern were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Vincent Kompany's return to the touchline.

According to recent reports, 'We will all try together to make this situation a positive one for ourselves. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too.'.

Bayern were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne, with Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore giving the visitors a shock first half lead at the Allianz Arena.

Nathaniel Brown drew Bayern level before half-time, but the hosts were unable to find a winner on Kompany's return.

The draw gives Borussia Dortmund the chance to move to the top of the Bundesliga table on Saturday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers' positive season continued on Sunday as they drew 2-2 with bitter rivals Burnley at Turf Moor.

Whilst there was some disappointment that Rovers couldn’t pick up three points to end the Clarets’ dominance in the fixture, it was a decent point on the road.

Plus, when you take into account the situation surrounding Tony Mowbray, who has sadly had to step back from leading the team due to health issues, the players deserve credit for the way they performed in such a big game.

It has been a team effort from Rovers during the campaign so far, although Andri Gudjohnsen deserves a special mention for his outstanding ability in front of goal.

But, he isn’t the only individual who could be picked out for praise, with Todd Cantwell having also shone for Blackburn, and he was particularly impressive against Burnley.

The 28-year-old, who was wearing the armband on Sunday, has established himself as a real leader at Ewood Park, and those qualities were on show in the derby game.

Not only did Cantwell step up to score a pressure penalty to make it 2-2, but he also put in a great all-round performance.

Plus, he has appeared to embrace the responsibility of becoming a crucial player for Rovers, and he has handled himself very well in terms of leading the tributes to Mowbray, which demonstrates he is a respected figure in the dressing room and at the club.

Having failed to kick-on and fulfil his potential after breaking through at Norwich, it’s good to see Cantwell is in a position where he appears to be enjoying his football again.

His final year or two at Carrow Road was a struggle, and Cantwell had a tough time at Rangers, who struggled to end Celtic’s domestic dominance during his period in Glasgow, and he didn’t always endear himself to supporters.

Yet, he has finally found a home at Blackburn, but Cantwell’s contract with Rovers is set to expire in the summer of 2027.

It has been claimed that the Championship side are hoping to agree fresh terms with the player, but, so far, an agreement has not been reached.

Therefore, this has to be an increasing concern for Blackburn, as Cantwell is going to have admirers, with previous reports stating that Wrexham and Derby were keen on the attacking midfielder.

Given his contract situation, you would expect further clubs to join the race for his signature, and he could be available for a cut-price in January.

The reality is that if Cantwell doesn’t sign a latest deal, Blackburn are going to risk losing him on a free if they don’t accept an offer in the New Year, which is likely to fall below his true value.

Some would argue that Rovers should keep Cantwell given they have a shot at reaching the play-offs, but losing someone like that on a free is bad business.

So, it goes without saying that Blackburn must prioritise keeping Cantwell, as that would undoubtedly be the best solution for the club.

Of course, every player has a price though, and if Cantwell’s wage demands are out of their reach, then the club will be in a difficult position.

It has been revealed that how vital is it for Blackburn to keep Todd Cantwell beyond January? Let us know in the comments below.

But, it is a chance for Venky’s to show some ambition, which has sadly been lacking regularly over the years.

If they can convince Cantwell to stay, it would add to the feel-good factor that has been built on the back of the great work that Mowbray has done this season, and he will be central to what they're trying to build moving forward.

Latest Update: Derby County fans slammed for "utterly ridiculous" David Clowes claims

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite pushing the Championship play-off places close in 2025-26, Derby County have been one of the big strugglers of the current campaign.
  • The Rams finished just four points adrift of the top six in May, but despite the backing in the transfer window of manager John Eustace, who was able to spend money on the likes of Bobby Clark, David Ozoh and Alex Mowatt, has struggled to get a tune out of his squad.
  • Injuries of course have not helped matters at Pride Park, but they sit inside the second tier relegation zone with Burnley and Preston North End, with no end in sight to their struggles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite pushing the Championship play-off places close in 2025-26, Derby County have been one of the big strugglers of the current campaign.

The Rams finished just four points adrift of the top six in May, but despite the backing in the transfer window of manager John Eustace, who was able to spend money on the likes of Bobby Clark, David Ozoh and Alex Mowatt, has struggled to get a tune out of his squad.

Injuries of course have not helped matters at Pride Park, but they sit inside the second tier relegation zone with Burnley and Preston North End, with no end in sight to their struggles.

Whilst the fanbase has been divided on Eustace's role as manager, with some wanting him gone and others blaming injuries for their rotten form as of late, chairman David Clowes is now getting it in the neck.

Local businessman Clowes rescued County in 2022 from administration, not long before they were close to liquidation after failing to find a buyer for some months, and just two years later, Derby were back in the Championship.

Clowes has made no secret about his search for external investment, but with Turki Alalshikh's buyout collapsing in August, it's left the 57-year-old on his own again.

And some Derby fans, like this one via X, are calling for Clowes to sell the club and depart to allow someone else to take them forward.

Whilst another believes that sticking with Eustace as manager and the results that have followed means that Clowes is ruining the legacy that he created a few years ago.

It's fair to say though that not every Rams fan is in agreement with the complaints and criticism that Clowes is getting.

When asked on the current situation at Pride Park right now, Football League World's Derby fan pundit, Shaun Woodward, believes that Clowes is getting an unnecessarily hard time from the fans.

"Some of the criticism David Clowes is receiving online is utterly ridiculous," Shaun told FLW.

"I'm not going to say that he should be immune to it, because he is the chairman of the club, and when a team is doing badly, the finger is going to be pointed at the manager and the chairman, it comes with the territory. I'm not going to sit here and say he should be immune from ever having any negativity thrown at him. We can't forever say because he saved the club, he's got a free pass, so to speak.

"But, the guy is a legend at Derby, and I do believe he deserves a little bit more respect on his name.

Clowes has Woodward's backing at Derby, and likely thousands of other fans, as it's not too long ago that he took a big risk to bring them out of liquidation danger.

Sources indicate that but it's clear to see that everything is not alright on the pitch. County are struggling to pick up points, and to the surprise of many from the start of the season that would've predicted them to be challenging for the top eight.

Many clubs would have changed manager by now, and whether or not Clowes is sticking by him or is being indecisive is a matter of opinion, but Woodward believes he needs to make the major call as soon as possible - whilst also being thankful that Clowes isn't another Mel Morris who throws his money around unnecessarily.

"Yes, he's making mistakes right now, and I do believe he should be getting rid of John Eustace, Stephen Pearce and quite a lot of the backroom staff - they don't seem to be doing their jobs," Shaun admitted.

"He should be surrounding himself with better footballing people that will make better decisions either with him or for him.".

"Who knows what is going on behind the scenes, I don't know whether he's actively out there trying to find those people, but it does seem at the moment that he is struggling to make a decision, and the longer we stay in this no man's land, where Pearce and Eustace are still around and we are losing every week, he's going to take a lot of flak.

"I still believe we should be thankful for what we have, and some of our fans have got short memories. We don't want to go back to the days of a Mel Morris-type chairman, who on the surface looked great by bringing in all these players, but behind the scenes he was lowering the club into the ground.

According to recent reports, does David Clowes need to sack John Eustace at Derby County? Comment below!

It has been revealed that "It's frustrating right now results-wise, but that to me is on John Eustace. I think Clowes has backed him the best he can, but he's probably struggling to make that big call about whether he should fire him or not, and I do feel for him.

But ultimately he's got to start making these big calls sooner rather than later, or he will continue to get some stick, but some of it is ridiculous in my opinion, and it needs to stop.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.

It has been revealed that at the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down. It’s called Jarrod Bowen, and I’m not entirely sure I’ve ever seen our captain play wider than he did at the London Stadium yesterday.

Sources indicate that what’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City. On that occasion, Parker was effectively handed a blueprint for getting the best out of West Ham’s most crucial player, yet we’ve barely seen it since.

During that extraordinary second-half comeback against Cardiff, Bowen was given a certain amount of freedom, perhaps encouraged by Parker or maybe he just took it upon himself to drift into the middle of the pitch and cause havoc.

Whatever the reason, he had a hand in all three West Ham goals, and the difference was remarkable.

For the first, he drifted into what might be regarded as the number 10 position and chipped a lovely ball over the Cardiff back line for Divine Mukasa to finish.

Sources indicate that the second was similar, with Bowen again creating the opening from a central position. His pass found Joël Piroe, whose flick released Arne Engels to score.

The third goal saw Bowen back in his more familiar position on the right-hand side, where he supplied a wonderful inswinging cross for Max Kilman to equalise.

Jarrod Bowen was given license to roam against Cardiff.

But that only went to show quite how much freedom Bowen had. In essence, he was everywhere.

As a blueprint, Scott Parker couldn’t have been given a better gift on his first day in charge than discovering that West Ham’s best player could operate with devastating effect from a free role.

Indeed, I was so encouraged by what I saw that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker must restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon following the defeat at Blackburn.

Because for a brief period against Cardiff, it looked as though we’d stumbled upon something rather special.

Therefore, I was a little underwhelmed that we didn’t see it repeated against Blackburn and very worried when we probably saw our captain more straightjacketed than ever against Preston North End.

If I could offer Parker one piece of encouragement or advice, it would be to get the best out of Bowen.

I’m quite sure our newly introduced head coach will improve the defence, and I think we saw signs of that yesterday, albeit against the league’s worst team.

But it can’t come at the expense of shackling our best player, who potentially could only be here for a few more months.

As I argued in my assessment of the Preston draw, West Ham had plenty of possession, shots and territory, but very little magic.

It has been revealed that and that’s the really bloody annoying part. We have a player who can provide exactly that, but we’re asking him to operate in a way which makes life considerably easier for the opposition.

According to recent reports, I know one thing. If I was head coach of an opposition Championship team and I saw Jarrod Bowen shackled to the right wing, I’d breathe a huge sigh of relief.

Because West Ham get one shot at this.

It has been revealed that if we don’t succeed in getting promotion, Bowen could leave for a pittance of £15m. That’s the release clause in the revised contract he agreed following relegation.

We do know that Bowen flew to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský before pledging to remain at West Ham for another season, as he explained in his interview with Sky Sports.

And I’m now very fearful that we are going to waste what should really be something of a cheat code for the division.

It has been revealed that bowen is comfortably our best attacking player, and we’ve already seen how devastating he can be when allowed to roam. Yet rather than building upon that discovery, Parker appears to have returned him to a position where he’s easier to mark and less able to influence the game.

I wish it weren’t so, but I’ve now come to the conclusion that the second half against Cardiff was a pure accident rather than a window into what we could begin to see from Scott Parker as he got his teeth into the West Ham job.

But decisions like that could well make the difference between automatic promotion and a play-off place, if we’re lucky.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER.

Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026.

Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney said her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she noted: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

Recent findings suggest that erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z.

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham.

It has been revealed that 'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'.

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

He said: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'.

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'.

They added that the VAR stated: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'.

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

Not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same.

An Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'.

A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X owners taking the opposite stance.

According to recent reports, one stated: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'.

Sources indicate that another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'.

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

24 hours on from West Ham’s  tepid point against the bottom side in the league and whilst the justified criticism is flying around, there are definitely positives to pull out of a fixture in which West Ham dominated all the notable statistics save the most important one: The points tally at the final whistle.

According to recent reports, sadly, again the Hammers have lost ground on the leaders and now sit eight points adrift. And yet, from Scott Parker’s comments, there are definite signs that he’s learned from at least some of the mistakes made by his predecessor. Reversing Nuno’s decision to cast out Edson Alvarez from the senior team proved a massive success.. Who knew.

Yesterday’s re-integration of ‘El Machin’ into the starting line up was his first league appearance in a West Ham shirt since May 2025.

This was an Alvarez playing more like his first season as a Hammer.

As Scott Parker summed up, Alvarez did not let him down:.

“He brought every bit of what we needed. It’s a young team, and his experience today in terms of organising and his general presence on the pitch was very, very good for us for large aspects.

“It was a major ask and I knew that going into the game, he hasn’t played at all this year and probably hasn’t had a lot of training in and around the first team. But I just felt his experience and know-how around it was needed, and for sure he was a massive part today of why we performed the way we performed” (Justin Allen- YouTube).

The Mexican clearly cares: He was in tears before kick off, so tough has his time in the football wilderness been.

Recent findings suggest that having been such a critic of him during his card-strewn Lopetegui era, credit where it is due. Edson Alvarez was, indeed, excellent yesterday and it is a testimony to his professionalism that he played a full ninety after not playing competitive football since August.

If he can maintain that kind of focus and form, Parker may well have found the missing piece in West Ham’s defensive jigsaw puzzle, that proved beyond his predecessor who simply wouldn’t extend the olive branch to any of his ‘frozen out’ players.

Forget Josh Brownhill - Birmingham City must target Bristol City ace in January

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Birmingham City have emerged as serious automatic promotion contenders this campaign under Chris Davies, and though their away defeat against Stoke City will have knocked morale, their ultimate goal remains the same.
  • Birmingham lost their place at the top of the Championship following their 1-0 away defeat to Stoke on Saturday, and in truth, Blues can have few complaints about the outcome, having been second best for the majority of the contest.
  • Head coach Davies will be keen to ensure this defeat doesn’t have any lasting effects on his group, as with this being just their third defeat in 16 league games, automatic promotion is still a real possibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City have emerged as serious automatic promotion contenders this campaign under Chris Davies, and though their away defeat against Stoke City will have knocked morale, their ultimate goal remains the same.

Birmingham lost their place at the top of the Championship following their 1-0 away defeat to Stoke on Saturday, and in truth, Blues can have few complaints about the outcome, having been second best for the majority of the contest.

Head coach Davies will be keen to ensure this defeat doesn’t have any lasting effects on his group, as with this being just their third defeat in 16 league games, automatic promotion is still a real possibility.

The January 2026 window allowed Davies to bring in the likes of August Priske, Carlos Vicente, Jhon Solis, and Ibrahim Osman, and looking ahead to the 2027 winter window, it would be no surprise to see Birmingham move with a similar purpose.

Each of Priske, Vicente, Solis, and Osman had a positive impact upon the Birmingham squad following their winter moves last January, and that has likely been kept in the back of Davies’ mind heading into the next January window.

Over the summer, according to TEAMtalk, Birmingham, alongside West Ham United, Southampton, Hull City, and Wrexham, were interested in bringing former Bristol City and Burnley midfielder Josh Brownhill back to England.

Brownhill, 30, amassed over 400 appearances across England’s top three tiers for the likes of Barnsley, Preston North End, Bristol City, and Burnley before joining Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Shabab in the summer of 2025.

The Englishman had just enjoyed a standout year in the Championship with the Clarets, scoring 18 and assisting six in 42 league appearances.

Unsurprisingly, clubs such as Birmingham and West Ham were sounding out the potential return of Brownhill, and whilst a move for the 30-year-old may be tempting, a more cost-effective move may already be in plain sight.

Brownhill’s ability is undoubted, and at 30, he is in and around his prime years as a professional footballer, but given the substantial wages he will undoubtedly be on in the Middle East, a return to England, especially the Championship, would come with a mighty pay cut.

With this, Birmingham should prepare to set their focus elsewhere, and continue their trend of interest in former Bristol City midfielders in the form of Irish international Jason Knight.

Knight, 25, has over 250 Championship appearances under his belt, having come through the ranks of Derby County, nailing down a place in the Rams’ side, before making the move to Ashton Gate in the summer of 2023, where he has been an almost ever-present under numerous coaches.

Whilst his performances haven’t quite been at the level he has previously shown to be capable of reaching this campaign under Michael Skubala, there is no denying his ability, and out of contract in the summer with no signs of penning an extension just yet, he could be available for cheap in January or nothing in the summer, as Birmingham must capitalise.

Knight can play anywhere across the midfield, or at right-back if required, though his favoured position is in the middle of the park, and he has established himself as one of the most consistent players in his role in the division over the past few years.

With Tomoki Iwata out of contract at St Andrews next summer, a successor in that role will be required, and on a free transfer, Knight would be an incredible pickup; linking up with former Derby and Bristol City teammate Max Bird in the Second City would also surely be tempting.

Taylor Gardener-Hickman is expected to leave in the summer as well, freeing up another role at right-back and midfield, which the Irishman could do so with aplomb.

At 25 and with an excellent injury record, Knight would be an incredible pickup for any second-tier side, and even if Birmingham were promoted, he could still play a role in the Premier League.

Five years younger than Brownhill and with room to develop even further, Knight is surely a no-brainer for Birmingham, who must turn their attention to Ashton Gate once again this winter.

Industry observers note that would you like to see Jason Knight at Birmingham this winter, or in the summer? Would you want Josh Brownhill to join instead, or as well as Knight? Share your thoughts below!

If Knight is reluctant to sign a new deal with Bristol City, it’s likely the Robins will prefer to sell for a cut-price this January rather than lose him for nothing in the summer, despite both scenarios being far from ideal, and Birmingham must take advantage.

Davies could do with a bit more bite and tenacity in the middle of the park, especially in the absence of Solis, who was on full display against Stoke, and Knight could offer just that.

His versatility would provide Davies with numerous different ways to deploy the Irishman, something he wouldn’t get with Brownhill, as the former Leicester City coach must ignore another move for Brownhill and pursue a deal for Knight instead.

💡 Key Takeaways
