  • Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and stated that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five.
  • "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

Industry observers note that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and stated that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

Recent findings suggest that but so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Sources indicate that neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

Sources indicate that it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

It has been revealed that we now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

Recent findings suggest that it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

In a recent development, "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their newly introduced head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

It has been revealed that united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

But, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

Recent findings suggest that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

It has been revealed that I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

According to recent reports, we wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a substantial team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so crucial for us.

In a recent development, there were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Industry observers note that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

In a recent development, it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

According to recent reports, it was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

Sources indicate that the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

Sources indicate that 5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm.

Fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

In a recent development, united break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

It has been revealed that united may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Sources indicate that manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

In a recent development, bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

According to recent reports, you would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

It has been revealed that here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Recent findings suggest that much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

Recent findings suggest that what a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”.

Industry observers note that well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

According to recent reports, fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the newly introduced season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

Sources indicate that more from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”.

Industry observers note that there has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Industry observers note that sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

In a recent development, at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

According to recent reports, fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

In a recent development, united’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Industry observers note that mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

Industry observers note that this stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

According to recent reports, fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

According to recent reports, bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

It has been revealed that josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Sources indicate that fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

In a recent development, fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

It has been revealed that bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

It has been revealed that A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Recent findings suggest that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

In a recent development, michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Sources indicate that subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

Recent findings suggest that the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a significant impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager remarked.

In a recent development, “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

It has been revealed that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty massive one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he mentioned it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

Industry observers note that the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

West Ham’s home problem summed up in one sentence – by a Preston fan

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Preston North End, the bottom side in the Championship, arrived in east London yesterday unaffected by the occasion and kept West Ham at bay for an hour until Dinos Mavropanos headed equaliser restored parity and saved Scott Parker’s blushes.

Two weeks’ work during the international break had accounted for very little as Preston withstood everything the Hammers and their almost 60,000 fans had to throw at their lowly opponents.

Recent findings suggest that and therein lies the problem. Having surrendered the small, intimidating, sometimes downright hostile atmosphere of Upton Park back in 2016, the distance from the pitch and the wide open spaces of the Olympic Stadium are about as intimidating as a day out at London Zoo for our opponents and their fans who continue to pour scorn on the venue.

In a recent development, it just doesn’t strike fear into opponents as it should. Even when we score.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium – as our opponents are finding out.

Preston fan Tm Mercer, writing in the Lancashire Evening Post, makes it abundantly clear that there was no noticeable crowd reaction to lift the home side, as there should have been once Mavropanos restored parity:.

“Aside from play-off finals, I’m pretty certain it is the first time I’ve been in a stadium for a league match with 60,000-plus through the gate.

Yet, when they equalised, it did not feel like the roar of that many people in such a cavernous ground. Give me somewhere like Gigg Lane, stood in their paddock pitch side, any day!”.

For the uninitiated, Gigg Lane is the home of Bury FC with a capacity of around…..12,000.

Recent findings suggest that nobody is suggesting the Hammers fans were silent. The cursèd accoustics from the soulless bowl and sheer distance from the pitch play right into opponents’ hands. And, ten years after moving in, it’s going to take a lot more than some safe standing and a couple of family zones to fix it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The January transfer window is on the horizon, and clubs in the Championship will already be looking at ways to strengthen their squads.

It’s a notoriously difficult month to do business, as clubs are reluctant to lose their key men midway through the campaign, which also means deals can come at a premium price.

However, there will be potential bargains out there, and one player who could fall into that category is ex-Celtic winger Liel Abada, who is currently playing with Charlotte FC in America.

The Israeli international is presently playing for Dean Smith’s side as they aim to win MLS Cup, and a 2-1 win over Chicago Fire last time out, where Abada scored, means they are in a good position to progress to the semi-final of the Eastern Conference.

Yet, it seems Abada’s future beyond this season is away from Charlotte, as Sky Sports reporter Lyall Thomas revealed that he is poised to leave when his contract expires next month.

That will end a three-season stay for Abada with the MLS outfit, and it’s fair to say he has had a mixed time of things.

Abada hasn’t always hit the heights expected of a designated player, but he has enjoyed his most productive campaign this time around, scoring 11 goals and registering five assists in 28 games.

Interestingly, the patch over Abada suggested that Wolves are among the clubs tracking the winger, although those reports have been played down elsewhere.

So, it will be intriguing to see how it develops, but Wolves are likely to be in the market for a newly introduced winger in January.

Cesar Peixoto has a good squad at his disposal, although Wanderers are lacking consistent end product from the likes of Mateus Mane and Rodrigo Gomes.

That means it’s an area they could look to address, and the prospect of signing Abada on a free transfer is something that may appeal, even if it has been mentioned that work permit issues could complicate a move for the 25-year-old, who may need to be loaned out initially.

Given Abada’s contract situation, it would be no surprise if a host of clubs were keeping tabs on the player.

He has done reasonably well for Charlotte over the years, and he hit double figures in consecutive years in Scotland, where he helped Celtic dominate domestically.

It has been claimed previously that Birmingham and Norwich were tracking the winger, so the opportunity to pick him up on a free transfer is likely to appeal.

With Abada capable of playing down both flanks, you could argue he would provide good depth for both clubs, who will fancy their chances of winning promotion this season.

When you consider Abada’s age, combined with the fact he will be available on a free, he is going to be a potential bargain for any club heading into January.

He does have flaws to his game, but Abada has proven regularly over the years that he can be a very good attacker.

Industry observers note that should your club sign Liel Abada? Let us know in the comments below.

At his best, he is a constant threat with his pace and ability to run in behind, whilst his movement and anticipation means he is often in the right place to score goals.

He was particularly impressive for Ange Postecoglou at Celtic at doing just that, which is why Charlotte FC paid around £8m to sign him.

So, this is someone with a good pedigree, and whilst January is a challenging month generally, Abada could prove to be a shrewd addition to any Championship club.

In a recent development, switching several key players after the international break was a brave move designed to revitalise West Ham’s fortunes. Had the ball not crashed against the woodwork four times but nestled in the corner just once we’d all be proclaiming his changes as astute: Bringing back Alvarez and switching Morato to a centre back role weren’t rocket science but shored up a hitherto leaky defence.

Recent findings suggest that however, bringing Fin Herrick into the side – ostensibly ‘resting’ (a.k.a.’dropping’) Hermansen – paid off . With Herrick now tried and tested, his elevation to credible first team keeper surely puts paid to any interest West Ham were showing in young Swansea ‘keeper Joe Duncan.

Herrick’s emergence means the budget doesn’t have to be diluted: Koppen can call off the search for a ‘keeper and find a goal scorer instead.

As Matt’s Claret and Hugh article last week predicted: “West Ham Could Save Themselves A Transfer Fee” by promoting Herrick rather than forking out millions to bring another promising young goal keeper to West Ham – when there’s one in situ already.

Exactly as it has seemed to pan out. Whilst Parker claims Hermansen has been strategically withdrawn for ‘some air’, there’s every chance that Herrick will get more match time whilst Areola remains unfit. And good luck to him. As he proved yesterday he’s got what it takes to keep a modest attack at bay.

A sterner test will come at Portsmouth but saving Koppen’s transfer budget for the acquisition of a striker who can actually hit the target looks to be the 100% absolute stone-cold priority in January, if it isn’t already too late.

And Herrick’s emergence has probably boosted the funds available to Koppen significantly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.
  • Recent findings suggest that ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break.
  • Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Recent findings suggest that ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

According to recent reports, while collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly substantial-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

It has been revealed that moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.
  • Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The new Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his upcoming surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he stated via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

Sources indicate that 'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6.

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their upcoming head coach.

The fresh Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'.

Industry observers note that in a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'.

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

Speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'.

The club then officially welcomed the latest manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

According to recent reports, 'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'.

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour.

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am.

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino).

Recent findings suggest that 'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'.

'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'.

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

Recent findings suggest that 'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something notable for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

Sources indicate that 'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made fresh friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'.

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

According to recent reports, ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Recent findings suggest that ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'.

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note.

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone.

Sources indicate that 'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino mentioned after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a upcoming contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship campaign is already nearing its halfway point, and many individuals have made headlines so far this season for differing reasons.

Several sides will now have one eye on achieving a play-off berth come May with the second tier table extremely congested, whilst for others, their immediate aim will be to stave off relegation to League One.

Of course, having a defence which is extremely tough to break down, as well as a combative midfield, can go a long way to achieving such short-term goals, but, ultimately, those at the top end of the pitch are paid top dollar for a reason.

Industry observers note that some of the Championship's forwards have already hit double-figures, and interest is already swirling over their services ahead of the January window, but are they among the 20 most valuable in the division according to Transfermarkt's current market values? Football League World take a look...

Sources indicate that this is list is NOT based on FLW's opinion, it's based on Transfermarkt's valuations. All figures converted from Euros to GBP.

Getting this list underway is Burnley's Swiss international forward, Zeki Amdouni.

The 25-year-old signed a five-year contract at Turf Moor in July 2023, but only recently hit a double-figure goal tally for the Clarets in just over 50 appearances.

At present, he holds a market value of £5.8m.

West Bromwich Albion's impressive start to the season has come about for many reasons, whilst Aune Heggebo continues to spearhead James Morrison's attack.

The Norwegian signed from SK Brann last summer for £4.75m, and his 13 goal contributions proved vital in the Baggies' eventual survival last term, before continuing to lead the line well alongside summer recruit, Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

Heggebo's market value has increased to £5.8m as a result.

However, one man whose market valuation has decreased to £5.8m is Sheffield United forward, Tom Cannon.

The five-time Republic of Ireland international set the Blades back a reported £10m from Leicester City in January 2025, but the striker's form has left such a figure rather unjustified.

Despite scoring six times last term, Cannon was the subject of reported summer interest, but remained in S2 and has since endured mixed runs of gametime.

The last striker on this list with a £5.8m market value is Birmingham City's highly-rated Dane, August Priske.

Recent findings suggest that priske, 22, signed from Djurgardens IF for £6m in January, and after an adaptation period, has started to come into his own at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

The well-rounded centre-forward is already closing in on a double-figure tally in all competitions despite missing a handful of games in recent weeks through injury.

George Hirst is the first of five strikers on this list with a current valuation of £6.6m.

This evening we feature a fan comment by Claret and Hugh reader ‘D” to highlight the considered alternative that perhaps, all is not doom and gloom just yet and that the new manager – whether or not he’s your own personal choice – deserves a fair chance to sort out his three predecessors’ combined cock ups.

I left that stadium yesterday thinking I must have watched a different game to many others, and then got back home about 7 to look online at various sites and saw exactly the same sort of rubbish.

The Terriers have already scored 28 goals so far this term with such a sharp front line, while they have also conceded the fewest goals in the division so far, a recipe for success when it comes to chasing promotion.

From their opening 15 league games, Martin Drury’s men have only tasted defeat twice so far this campaign, with eight victories in the process, leaving them in a handy position to challenge and get into top spot over the festive period.

However, there is big competition and several sides eyeing up a place in the top two themselves, with Oxford United only losing once all season and chasing an instant return to the Championship, while the same can be mentioned for Sheffield Wednesday, who appear rejuvenated under Dave Challinor and are just three points off the Terriers.

Versatile enough to flip between playing as a number 10 and as a lone striker, Taylor has already got into double figures for goals from the 14 league games he’s played in, nailing himself down as one of the first names on the team sheet due to such a clinical nature in the final third.

In what will be a scare for Huddersfield Town supporters, Joe Taylor has been linked with leaving Huddersfield Town in January and making a move to the Championship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Industry observers note that despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

Sources indicate that A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In a recent development, in danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

According to recent reports, the outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

Industry observers note that it’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

On Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Industry observers note that kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

Recent findings suggest that mcCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

In a recent development, jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Recent findings suggest that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

Industry observers note that O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager demonstrated up well.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.
  • Recent findings suggest that around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel.
  • The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Recent findings suggest that around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his new squad, but its release quickly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator mentioned the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He mentioned: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its newly introduced head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scott Parker’s decision to recall Soungoutou Magassa from the ‘Nuno wilderness’ back into the West Ham fold looks well founded.

Similarly, the apparent re-integration of Edson Alvarez into West Ham United’s starting eleven last weekend has been met with almost universal approval after the Mexican’s decent showing against Preston.

Sources indicate that at the very least, these two players will see their transfer values rise simply by being deployed in competitive football. At best, they could contribute significantly towards a successful outcome for the club this season.

All of which makes Niclas Fullkrug’s escapades in Germany even more ironic, as West Ham’s failure to score their winner after thirty attempts gets put into sharp relief by their on-loan striker becoming the Bundesliga’s top scorer.

Another goal by Fullkrug at the weekend in Bremen’s 4- 0 victory will make Hammers fans scratch their head and wonder whether, with different coaching and different attitudes, the German could have made an impact in east London this season. He’d certainly have got some game time.

Fullkrug is now the top scorer in the German league after his ninth goal for Werder Bremen at the weekend.

Too late to think about recalling Fullkrug, it seems he’s found his spiritual ‘home’, and good luck to him.

It does throw the coaching failures of the last three of West Ham’s so called ‘managers’ sharply into focus when they all relied heavily on their favourites and ‘fell out’ frequently with players: Who can forget Lopetegui’s dressing room bust-ups with Mohammed Kudus and Jean-Clair Todibo?

Eye-watering sums are spent by football clubs on researching, scouting and recruiting players, but then whole careers seem ended on a managerial whim or a clash of egos.

By no means unique to West Ham, but it is an area in which clubs have to learn to do better or risk losing, as in Fullkrug’s case, the very stars who can fire the goals they’ve just paid through the nose to acquire.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

Recent findings suggest that “Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

Industry observers note that manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a significant reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring matter with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of significant trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in major games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

In a recent development, “Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

Sources indicate that pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

In a recent development, the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

The fresh Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino stated in his first Manchester United press conference.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he remarked.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

Tech Report: Top 9 friendliest EFL League Two fanbases named and ranked by AI

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football fandom can shine through in many different ways with many clubs throughout Europe and beyond taking pride in creating a hostile and difficult atmosphere for their opponents.
  • Hooliganism, born in England with the so-called ‘English disease’ is something that can get confused with that desire for hostility and an intimidatory atmosphere but it must be remarked English football and the passion of its supporters in that regard has dwindled in the last 30 years or so.
  • Regardless of that, though, the sheer depth of the English football pyramid and large crowds as low as the eighth and ninth tiers, unparalleled across the world, is something that remains a source of pride for English football supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football fandom can shine through in many different ways with many clubs throughout Europe and beyond taking pride in creating a hostile and difficult atmosphere for their opponents.

Hooliganism, born in England with the so-called ‘English disease’ is something that can get confused with that desire for hostility and an intimidatory atmosphere but it must be remarked English football and the passion of its supporters in that regard has dwindled in the last 30 years or so.

Regardless of that, though, the sheer depth of the English football pyramid and large crowds as low as the eighth and ninth tiers, unparalleled across the world, is something that remains a source of pride for English football supporters.

Attracting huge crowds lower down the leagues can be reliant upon a variety of factors but a crucial couple involve the welcoming and community-like nature of a fanbase.

The fourth-tier is the best mix of English football with some fairly big spending and ambitious ‘new’ clubs in the EFL that have risen up from non-league, old and storied outfits wanting to restore their reputation and teams punching above their weight by even being in England’s top four divisions.

As a result, we have consulted AI chatbot ChatGPT to rank the nine friendliest fanbases in League Two. It could even be that many clubs pride themselves on having a more unwelcoming and hostile atmosphere, too, to try and rattle the opposition – and so this may not be the most overly positive ranking that it first appears, albeit all of that and what it feels and how it is perceived also remains subjective.

Recent findings suggest that first up on the list, the ninth friendliest fanbase in League Two, according to AI, are Cheltenham Town’s supporters. Down in Gloucestershire, The Robins have been deemed to have such a ‘relaxed’ and ‘friendly match day experience’ that they are among the friendliest fans in the fourth-tier.

Under the management of Steve Cotterill, Cheltenham will be expecting to be steady enough by the spring that they can have a tilt at the top seven and the play-off places. The Gloucestershire-based outfit have reconnected with supporters after a difficult couple of years.

In the heart of Lancashire, it may be stereotypical for Accrington Stanley supporters to be the archetypal friendly Lancastrians but they are ranked eighth on the list by AI. A fun away day, the ‘close knit community’, as described by ChatGPT, marks Stanley out as having one of the friendliest fanbases in League Two.

Accrington have punched above their weight pretty much throughout their history and they are again doing so this season with a fun to watch team in England’s fourth-tier. The openness of owner Andy Holt has also helped Accrington form their connection with supporters, albeit some did become critical of Holt’s outspoken nature on social media.

Once again up in the North West for ChatGPT’s list, Crewe Alexandra have been deemed the seventh friendliest fanbase in League Two with the AI chatbot describing The Alex has having a ‘community feel’ and a ‘welcoming atmosphere’. It is often another fun away day, too, with Gresty Road right by Crewe train station, hence their The Railwaymen nickname.

Having been League Two play-off finalists in the 2023-24 campaign, Crewe look to be back towards the level of that team this time around with Lee Bell’s side pushing for promotion once again.

Whether travelling from below the midlands north or vice versa, the Bescot Stadium is famous for its ubiquity in terms of being spotted on a longer away day for supporters. The home of Walsall has also been marked out as the home of the sixth friendliest fanbase in League Two with AI suggesting The Saddlers boast a family-friendly fanbase.

Walsall supporters remained patient in recent years with successive collapses away from promotion, having been top at Christmas in both of the last two seasons, and they have been rewarded with another strong side but nothing can be taken for granted.

Sources indicate that back in the EFL, York City have been inserted as the fifth friendliest fanbase in League Two according to AI. The Minstermen, now at the York Community Stadium since 2021 after moving from Bootham Crescent, have managed to maintain a ‘passionate fanbase’ despite that move, as suggested by ChatGPT, and that has them in the top five for the chatbot.

Like many clubs coming straight up from the National League in recent seasons, York are putting themselves in the promotion picture in League Two with that fervent fanbase behind them.

Ranked fourth in ChatGPT’s list of friendliest fanbases, Chesterfield are up next. According to AI, The Spireites have ‘strong connection’ with their supporters and the local community and ‘excellent support’, as it explains, marks it out as one of the friendlier groups of supporters – and being able to see the famous crooked spire from the away end is also a bit of a boon.

National League winners in the 2023-24 campaign, Chesterfield have been play-off semi-finalists in each of the last two seasons with a now patient Chesterfield fanbase hoping to take the next step this time around.

According to recent reports, heading into the top three, ChatGPT has ranked Merseyside outfit Tranmere Rovers as having one of the friendliest fanbases in League Two. Described as being a ‘traditional club’ by AI, Tranmere are stated to have a ‘welcoming culture’ that has the chatbot putting them third in this list.

Tranmere are a steadily run club and will hope to punch themselves clear of the fourth-tier this season, having survived relegation on the final day last season, as they push towards the top seven and the play-off places.

Industry observers note that up to second on the list of the friendliest fanbases in League Two are Grimsby Town – which Manchester United supporters may disagree with given the way in which The Mariners fans managed to help their side overwhelm and eventually produce one of the EFL Cup’s biggest upsets last season. Those ‘passionate’ fans, as explained by AI, are described as being able to create a ‘fantastic atmosphere’ with Grimsby’s travelling support also given as a reason for Town being so high on the list.

Dave Artell is one of the most well-regarded coaches in the EFL and, after missing out in the League Two play-off semi-finals last season, Grimsby will be hopeful of pushing themselves into the third-tier this year with the backing of an impressive fanbase, both in terms of their support and attitude – according to AI.

According to recent reports, and now we come to the top of the list with AI chatbot ChatGPT deeming Gillingham to have the friendliest fanbase in League Two. According to ChatGPT, Gillingham are described as having ‘loyal supporters’ with a ‘strong community’ between the club and players marking them out as top spot in this list in Kent, a county self-anointed as ‘England’s back garden’.

Many away supporters may find it a surprise that Gillingham rank so high on this list with the narrow streets leading up to the Priestfield Stadium occasionally presenting quite an intimidatory build up if circumstances dictate, perhaps on a game-by-game basis. AI has opted not to take that into consideration in its ranking though.

Gills have started steadily and will want to find themselves in the hunt for a promotion challenge again in the fourth-tier, under the management of Gareth Ainsworth, and they will hope to be one of League One’s friendliest fanbases next season, well, at least one of the friendliest fanbases in the eyes of an AI chatbot next season.
